Directions for Questions 96 to 100:
Read the passage carefully and answer the questions that follow:
"The fundamental bedrock of civil society rests upon the maintenance of an impartial and accessible judiciary. When
legal redress becomes an exorbitant luxury or is bogged down in chronic procedural procrastination, citizens lose
faith in institutional justice. The adage 'justice delayed is justice denied' reflects not merely an abstract moral
critique, but an economic and sociological reality. A backlog of millions of pending litigations ties up capital,
discourages commercial investments, and undermines the rule of law. Judicial efficiency therefore requires
structural streamlining, comprehensive technological integration, and continuous procedural reforms to ensure
speedy and equitable dispensation of justice to all strata of society."
questions.questionText: What forms the fundamental bedrock of civil society according to the passage?
